newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate Republicans support arts body.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate Republicans support arts body.

text.p: Key Senate Republicans said Tuesday they will back the National Endowment for the Arts (NEA), which conservatives want to dismantle.

Jim Jeffords, a Vermont Republican and chairman of the Labour Committee that oversees the NEA, told the NEA chairman, actress Jane Alexander, he was confident the body would survive. He was joined by Virginia Republican John Warner.

"I am confident that we will be able to move forward this Congress and craft legislation that addresses concerns, yet allows the agencies to continue to fufill their mission of increasing access to the arts and humanities," Jeffords said at a hearing on the NEA's future.

Republican support is crucial for the NEA because House Speaker Newt Gingrich has joined a large group of conservatives who are campaigning to kill the programmes, which provide financial support for the arts.
Congress slashed the NEA's budget by about 40 percent to $99 million a year for 1996 and 1997. President Clinton has proposed increasing spending to $136 million.
Gingrich told reporters earlier this month that big stars who campaign to preserve the agency should fund it themselves, an idea that Alexander called "elitist."
